reuse.why: The change reuses recurrence conversion and date adjustment helpers, but the range handler independently implements the daily skip policy.

duplication.why: Daily skip eligibility is repeated between getNextDate and getDatesInRange, and the range handler repeats the new isNonBusinessDay predicate.

placement.why: Holiday matching belongs in shared schedules code, but the server handler also owns scheduling policy that should be shared with other consumers.

scope.why: All edits directly support the requested scheduling rules, range handler, configuration field, and associated tests.

maintainability.why: Maintainers must coordinate multiple policy implementations and holiday argument propagation, while the range handler additionally embeds its own adjustment-padding assumption.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getDatesInRange in server/schedules/app.ts spells out weekend-or-holiday detection instead of sharing isNonBusinessDay from shared/schedules.ts.

disguised_duplication.where: getDatesInRange reshapes getNextDate's daily skip policy into an inline continue branch and expands isNonBusinessDay into d.isWeekend(date) || isHoliday(date, config.holidays).

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter; getNextDate gains a daily-specific skip path; the new getDatesInRange consumer independently implements that policy, while getUpcomingDates and budget schedule-template retain separate adjustment orchestration.
